title: Tioram
instruction: Lägg brickor i ramen — och se hur mycket plats som är kvar.
gateBody: Ett bibliotek med färdiga ramar — samma tal lagt på fem sätt, tiokamraterna, par att jämföra och talen elva till nitton både i en ram och i två. Och dina egna ramar sparade — kvar till nästa lektion.
_notes: DEFINITE-FORM SCREEN — every noun we ship, in indefinite and definite singular and plural, read aloud. (1) ram / ramen / ramar / ramarna. ⚠ FLAGGED AND ACCEPTED: 'ramen' is spelt identically to the Japanese noodle dish, now an everyday Swedish loanword (ramennudlar, ramenrestaurang). We rule it NON-hazardous, and the ruling is not a shrug: unlike the recorded 'skriv ut banan' case, 'ramen' never appears inside an imperative and never appears without the apparatus visible beside it, and the tool announces itself as Tioram. It is also UNAVOIDABLE — the title is locked to Tioram and the frame cannot be called anything but the frame. Do not 'fix' this later by renaming the part. (2) bricka / brickan / brickor / brickorna — safe, and see the COUNTER note for why we never use the definite singular. (3) ask / asken / askar / askarna — safe; the only homograph is 'ask' the ash TREE (definite also 'asken'), which is botanical, benign and impossible to reach in a maths context. (4) rad / raden — safe. (5) plats / platsen — safe, and it is a mass noun here, not a named part. (6) tal / talet — safe, standard school register.

TRAY — 'asken', and the census forced it. ⚠⚠ 'brickan' is REFUSED outright: in shipped Swedish 'bricka' is the COUNTER in four tools (part-whole-frame:89,98 · sound-boxes:37,85 · word-builder-core:37 · choice-board-core:32) and simultaneously the TRAY in fraction-kitchen (:63 'Fyll brickan', :71 'Brickan — beviset…'). Calling our tray 'brickan' would collide with our own counters inside a single sentence. 'burken' REFUSED — jar is owned three times over (estimation-jar is the entire tool, name-sticks:36,42,75, class-timer:80 'Sandburk'). 'skålen' REFUSED — measurement-bench:69,74 ('den breda skålen', 'vågskålen') and number-balance's pans. 'lådan' REFUSED — letter-tiles:79, and 'hela verktygslådan' is a live PLAN NAME in place-value-lab:73-75 and picture-word-wall:91-94. 'facket' REFUSED even though it collides with no tool: in adult Swedish 'facket' is overwhelmingly the trade union, and this string is read aloud to a teacher by a screen reader. 'asken' is what Swedish classroom counters actually come in ('en ask med brickor'), it is unclaimed across all 47 tools, and it is common gender, so the empty state is 'tom' and not 'tomt'. This replaces the draft's 'Facket' in all three tray keys.

DEFECT (EN source) — TRAY HAD NO SINGULAR, AND ONE COUNTER IS THE PEDAGOGICALLY LOADED STATE. RESOLVED UPSTREAM DURING THIS PANEL. 'The tray — {n} counters left' rendered '1 counters left'; the draft Swedish 'Facket — {n} brickor kvar' rendered '1 brickor kvar', which is simply ungrammatical. There was a trayEmptyAria for 0 and nothing for 1 — and 1 is the exact moment the whole tool is built around (one more to full). German dodged it by accident, because 'Plättchen' is invariant in the plural; Swedish, Dutch, the Romance locales and the other Nordics cannot. While we worked, the source gained trayAriaOne and ten-frame.js gained the branch (left<=0 → empty, left===1 → trayAriaOne, else trayAria, :1050-1052) — we VERIFIED the branch exists rather than assuming the key was wired, because an added key with no code path is just a new dead string. Because the singular is now handled, trayAria is guaranteed n>=2 and can take the natural plural 'Asken — {n} brickor kvar'; our earlier number-neutral workaround ('{n} kvar att lägga i') is no longer needed and would now be the weaker string, since it withholds the noun from a screen-reader user.

DEFECT (code, a11y) — STILL OPEN, AND WE BELIEVE IT IS UNREPORTED: UNDER THE PAIRS ORDER THIS COUNTING TOOL STOPS COUNTING WHEN IT IS READ ALOUD. Cell labels are the ORDINAL (:1015-1017, String(i+1)) while the arrow keys move by VISUAL POSITION, which the code states as a deliberate choice (:803-805). Under order:'pairs', posOf maps k → r=k%2, c=floor(k/2) (:543-545), so the top row holds ordinals 0,2,4,6,8 and a screen-reader user arrowing right along it hears '1, 3, 5, 7, 9'. The same happens under upright, which transposes the grid. The comment at :1010-1014 asserts the benefit that 'a serial read of 7-of-10 becomes 1 counter, 2 counter, … 7 counter, 8, 9, 10' — that claim holds ONLY under the default order:'rows' with upright:false, i.e. in one of four setting combinations, and the file asserts it unconditionally. In a tool whose entire subject is cardinality, hearing 1,3,5,7 for four counters is worse than hearing nothing. Fix by labelling from the visual reading position, or scope the comment and accept it — but it should not stand as written. Not fixable from the string set.

DEFECT (code) — DEAD STRING routinesBtn. RESOLVED UPSTREAM DURING THIS PANEL. It was authored in all eleven locales at ten-frame.js:269 and referenced ZERO times in the file (grep -c = 1, the declaration itself); _buildBar (:1065-1189) builds the field chips, Ordna, Fyll resten, Skriv ut and Keeps and nothing else. This was the #39 hintMark / #44 hintTurn class again, in a build whose header advertises a reachability discipline. It has since been deleted from BOTH _source-en.json and ten-frame.js, so we do not ship a value for it and the key set matches the source exactly. Recorded for whoever revives a Routines control: do NOT call it 'Serier' in Swedish. Bare 'serier' reads first as COMICS (serietidningar), which is precisely why both shipped siblings compound it — rekenrek:62 'Kulserier', number-talk-easel 'Bildserier'. 'Ramserier' is the Swedish form. ⚠ The da and no drafts still carried the bare 'Serier' and want the same check if the key returns.

DEFECT (EN source, tier truth) — gateBody SOLD A FREE FEATURE. RESOLVED UPSTREAM DURING THIS PANEL. It used to end '…and print the one on screen', but Print is deliberately NOT gated: the chip at :1162-1169 carries no entitlement check at all and the header records it as operator-ruled ('never gate the first affordance', this being TOOL_KEYS[0]). A paid gate advertising what a signed-out teacher already has is worse than a thin gate, and the sheet is BLANK in every tier anyway (:1354-1356), so no filled-frame reading rescues the claim. The source now ends 'Keep the frames you build and come back to them.' Our Swedish gateBody was written without the print clause and needs no change; it promises only the prepared library and Keeps.

DEFECT (EN source) — A FOURTH NAMED PART. RESOLVED UPSTREAM DURING THIS PANEL. The header states the tool has three nouns — THE FRAME, THE COUNTER, THE TRAY — 'and nothing else in this tool gets a noun', yet fieldTwentyField said 'Field of TWENTY' while its four sibling chips all said 'Frame' and the grid's own accessible name is 'The frame'. That was the #41 'the bench was a fourth named part in a three-part tool' defect verbatim. The source now reads 'Frame of twenty'. Our Swedish had already refused the fourth noun independently: the draft 'Tjugofält' was rejected both as a fourth part AND as a coinage no Swedish teacher says (Sweden has no Zwanzigerfeld tradition to name), and we ship 'Tjugo i en ram', which introduces no new noun and carries the distinction that actually matters straight to the teacher — 'Tjugo i EN ram' against 'TVÅ tioramar'. This now aligns exactly with the corrected English.

DEFECT (product lexicon, Swedish) — STILL OPEN: THE PAID PLAN HAS THREE DIFFERENT SWEDISH NAMES IN SHIPPED TOOLS. 'Lärarpaketet' (part-whole-frame gateBand/gateWays/gatePrint/unlock), 'hela verktygslådan' (place-value-lab:73-75, picture-word-wall:91-94) and plain 'Premium' (rekenrek, number-talk-easel, measurement-bench, class-timer, estimation-jar). A Swedish teacher who meets two of our tools meets two products. We follow the brief and the newest sibling — gateCta is 'Se Lärarpaketet', byte-identical to part-whole-frame's unlock string — and flag the other two families for normalisation. A locale panel cannot fix this from one JSON.

DEFECT (code, a11y) — STILL OPEN: ONE ACCESSIBLE NAME ON SEVERAL CONTROLS. frameAria is set on both the counter grid (:663) and the field-chooser radiogroup (:1073), so 'Ramen' names two unrelated controls; keepsBtn names the Keeps chip (:1179), the '+' button (:1295) AND every saved board (:1309), so a teacher with twelve Keeps meets thirteen controls all called 'Mina ramar'. Related and smaller: frameAria and numeralAria are grammatically singular ('Ramen', 'I ramen') while labelling a stage that holds TWO frames under twentypair — which is the Swedish default. We keep the singular because the name must stay geometry-neutral and short, and we record it. None of this is fixable from the string set; it needs new keys.

COUNTER — 'Brickor', confirmed against the platform rather than chosen. It is the shipped Swedish counter noun in four tools (see the TRAY note). 'Plockisar' rejected: real Swedish preschool slang for manipulatives, but regional and too infantile for åk 2. 'Marker' / 'markörer' rejected as calques. 'Knappar' (buttons) rejected: it would collide with the UI buttons the tool is made of. Note the discipline this also enforces — because 'brickan' is fraction-kitchen's tray, we use the definite singular nowhere in this set; our forms are 'Brickor' (indefinite plural), 'en bricka' (indefinite singular) and 'brickor' inside trayAria.

TIDY — 'Ordna'. It is the verb an åk-1 teacher says to a scattered set ('nu ordnar vi brickorna'), it is one word on a chip, and it is directionally neutral. 'Sortera' REJECTED, and the reason is mathematical rather than stylistic: sorting is classification by attribute, a different verb owned by other surfaces, and nothing here is being classified. 'Städa' REJECTED: it is the put-the-toys-away word and implies the counters LEAVE, which is the exact opposite of what snap() does — snap is count-preserving (:441-445), and the announcement's whole job is to say so. 'Räta upp' rejected as too physical (straightening something bent). 'Samla ihop' rejected: it predicts a pile, not a canonical arrangement.

ORDER LABEL — 'Så fylls ramen', and the reason is a collision inside our own set. The obvious label is 'Ordning', which sits one letter from the Tidy chip 'Ordna' and would have a teacher reading a drawer setting and a stage control as the same word. 'Ordningsföljd' (the exact equivalent of da 'Rækkefølge' / no 'Rekkefølge') shares the same root and is stiff. 'Så fylls ramen' says what the setting does, uses only the tool's own head noun, and matches shipped house style for descriptive setting labels (measurement-bench 'Linjalkoll efter räkningen', rekenrek 'Rader per ram' and 'Säg talet vid Ta fram').

UPRIGHT — 'Ställ på högkant' replaces the draft's 'Ställ på höjden'. 'På höjden' means in the height dimension / portrait aspect and is what you say about a photograph, not about standing an object on its end. 'På högkant' is the fixed Swedish idiom for exactly this move, it is what the da and no siblings say ('på højkant' / 'på høykant'), and 'ställa något på högkant' is a phrase any Swedish adult uses without thinking.

COMPLEMENT — 'tiokamraterna' CONFIRMED, and we think it is the strongest single word in this locale's copy. It is the established term in Swedish maths didactics for the partners to ten and it is what a Swedish teacher types into a search box; 'tiokompisar' is the folksier regional variant, and 'talkamrater' is the generic superordinate (partners to any number), so neither carries the ten. The calque 'partner till tio' is not Swedish. ⚠ Note the trap it avoids, which is the one German records too: the adjacent-looking Swedish term is 'tiotalsövergång', the make-ten STRATEGY — that is refusal #17 and a fence the header records as having five owners, so it appears nowhere in our copy. For the teens clause we therefore say plainly 'talen elva till nitton', which asserts nothing about crossing.

KEEPS — 'Mina ramar'. This is the shipped house shape for a paid save-shelf across three Swedish siblings: rekenrek 'Mina serier', number-talk-easel 'Mina serier', measurement-bench 'Mina gissningar'. The draft's 'Sparade ramar' is longer on a chip and past-participial where the siblings are possessive. It also matches the four locales that already chose 'my frames' (fr 'Mes cadres', it 'I miei quadri', es 'Mis marcos', pt 'Meus quadros'), and it stays distinct from gateTitle 'Fler ramar' at a glance.

saidFull — 'Nu är det fullt', and this is a homograph screen result, not a style preference. ⚠⚠ The direct rendering 'Full — 10 av 10' is REFUSED: bare sentence-initial 'full' in spoken Swedish reads first as DRUNK ('han är full'), and this string is announced aloud into a classroom. The impersonal neuter 'det är fullt' cannot carry that reading at all — the drunk sense is personal and common-gender — and 'nu är det fullt' is what a Swedish teacher actually says about a container that has filled up. It carries a second benefit we needed anyway: being impersonal, it does not have to agree with a stage that is ONE frame under twentyfield and TWO under twentypair.

saidTidied — 'Fortfarande {n} av {cap} — nu i ordning'. Its whole job is to state the invariant, and 'Fortfarande {n} av {cap}' does that in the first three words, before the reason for the announcement arrives. ⚠ We deliberately avoided naming the counters here: 'brickorna är ordnade' is plural-marked and would be ungrammatical at n=1, which is reachable (one counter sitting at cell 8; Tidy moves it to cell 1 and announces). 'Nu i ordning' is number-neutral.

GEOMETRY RULING (sv) — sv STAYS ON `default`, i.e. twenty = 'twentypair', two tioramar. This is a positive ruling from this panel and not an unexamined inheritance: Swedish classroom materials present twenty as two ten-frames, and Sweden has no Zwanzigerfeld tradition equivalent to the German one — there is not even a settled Swedish noun for a 2x10 field, which is precisely why our chip has to DESCRIBE it ('Tjugo i en ram') rather than name it. Both fields stay available, as the code intends. No change to GEOMETRY_BY_LOCALE is required.

REGISTER — du throughout, INCLUDING the gate, and this is where Swedish parts company with the German panel. German kept its gate personless because du to a teacher in paid copy is a register slip; in Swedish, after du-reformen, there is no polite alternative — 'ni' to a single teacher reads archaic or faintly hostile — so personless copy would read cold rather than respectful. 'dina egna ramar' is correct B2C Swedish addressed to a teacher. The instruction is child-directed imperative, matching every shipped Swedish manipulative (rekenrek:41 'Skjut kulorna', part-whole-frame:89 'Flytta en bricka', measurement-bench 'Gissa först, mät sedan').

INSTRUCTION — 'se' replaces the draft's 'titta': 'titta hur mycket…' is ungrammatical without 'på', and 'se hur mycket plats som är kvar' is the natural clause. We kept the ROOM framing over the tray framing ('se hur många som är kvar i asken') for the reason the header itself gives: on paper, ink and white are equally present, but on a screen the empty cells read as background, so the ghost is the half that needs the words. The ask can be seen without being named.

SIBLING COLLISION, unavoidable, DOCUMENTED — rekenrek.js:43 ships sv racksLabel = 'Ramar', and :49/:58 use 'varje ram' and 'Ramen är gömd bakom ridån' for a rekenrek rack. So the bare noun 'ram' is claimed by two tools. It cannot be subtracted here per §23.3: both head terms are compounds in -ram (Tioram, Kulram), our title is LOCKED, and no other Swedish word names a ten-frame. Mitigation — the two are never on screen together, rekenrek's own head term is Kulram, and the weaker claim is rekenrek's, since a rekenrek's units are stänger and rader (it already ships rodAria 'Kulstång' and setRows 'Rader per ram'). If anything moves later, move rekenrek's racksLabel, not this.

SOFT OVERLAPS, accepted — 'ruta' (cell) is owned by sound-boxes:37 and word-builder-core:37; we never name our cells, which are labelled by bare ordinal, so there is nothing to subtract. 'rad' appears in fieldTenRow and orderRows and also in rekenrek's rowsNote, but a row describes an arrangement rather than being one of the tool's three named parts — the de panel set the same precedent with 'Zehn in einer Reihe' / 'Reihe für Reihe'. 'Visa talet' is shared verbatim with rekenrek:46 and is the same affordance, so sharing it is consistency, not collision.

TITLE == fieldTen, accepted. In Swedish both are 'Tioram', so the tool name and one chip name coincide. This is not a Swedish slip — de (Zehnerfeld), nl (Tienraam), da and no (Tierramme) all ship the same identity, because in each of those languages the head term for the ten-frame IS the name of the ten-field. Renaming the chip would mean not calling the ten-frame a ten-frame. Confirmed also against number-talk-easel:63, which already ships sv reprTenframe = 'Tioram' and reprDouble = 'Dubbel tioram' — our lexicon matches the platform's existing Swedish term for this representation.

OBSERVED IN PASSING (other locales, the interim draft in ten-frame.js) — trayAriaOne and trayAria use DIFFERENT tray nouns in fr ('La barquette' vs 'Le plateau') and es ('La reserva' vs 'La bandeja'), i.e. the tool acquires two names for one object between two adjacent announcements. Those panels may already have fixed it in their own JSON; flagged only because it is visible from here and cheap to check.

CHECKED — key set and key ORDER identical to _source-en.json (31 keys), verified programmatically against the applier's own KEYS/NEEDS/INVISIBLE/LOCKED_TITLE tables rather than a reimplementation of them. No verdict, score, praise or correctness word (rätt, fel, bra jobbat, poäng, duktig) anywhere; the bans were poison-tested in BOTH directions, so that 'rätt' fires on 'det blev rätt' and does NOT fire on 'rättvis'. No string demands an answer: no 'svar'/'svara', no 'skriv talet', and no question mark in any of the 31 values ('Skriv ut' is the shipped print chip, verbatim from part-whole-frame, and is not an instruction to write a number). Placeholders present and correctly spelt in exactly the eight keys that require them and in no others; {cap} appears twice in saidFull as the code's global replace expects, and {n} and {left} appear at most once per string as _say's non-global replace requires. No soft hyphen, no non-breaking space, no zero-width character; em dash U+2014 with a plain space each side, matching the shipped Swedish siblings. ⚠ NOTE FOR THE ORCHESTRATOR: _source-en.json changed TWICE while this panel worked (31 keys with routinesBtn → 30 with it deleted → 31 with trayAriaOne added, plus edits to fieldTwentyField and gateBody). This file is written against the state at the end of that sequence, and every claim above was re-measured after the last change.
